concerns.text: Task T037 attempts to download the 'NAB' (Numenta Anomaly Benchmark) dataset as a fallback for the Z-Reward dataset. The spec (FR-001) and Constitution (Principle VI) explicitly require the Z-Reward dataset with four specific rubric dimensions (Alignment, Realism, Aesthetics, Plausibility). NAB contains time-series anomaly data and lacks these dimensions. This task silently relaxes the data source requirement, making FR-001 and US-1 impossible to satisfy with the specified data structure.

Task T022b defines the 'Dominant Eigenvalue' calculation as a 'Global Covariance Matrix' computed across the 'entire dataset' (population-level), resulting in a single scalar. Spec FR-002 and US-2 Independent Test require calculating the dominant eigenvalue 'for each sample' to derive the per-sample entanglement score. This task weakens the requirement from a per-sample feature vector to a global constant, violating the spec's demand for per-sample predictors for the Random Forest (FR-004).

Task T030c explicitly instructs the implementer 'DO NOT mandate a t-test if assumptions are violated' when comparing against the null baseline. Spec SC-002 requires measuring 'statistically significant improvement (p < 0.05 via paired t-test)'. This task silently relaxes the verification method defined in the success criteria, potentially allowing the project to pass without the required statistical validation.

Task T037 includes a 'tertiary' fallback to a local file 'data/raw/artificialWithAnomaly.csv' if remote sources fail. Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) mandates that results be reproducible on a fresh runner without manual intervention. Relying on a local file that is unlikely to exist in a fresh CI environment violates this constitutional principle and creates a non-reproducible execution path.
